items.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 1 at 1:20PM EST until November 3 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Miami FL
items.description:
* WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.
For the Coastal Flood Advisory, moderate coastal flooding.

* WHERE...Coastal Miami Dade County.

* WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, through Tuesday evening.
For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 7 PM EST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected. Rip currents can sweep even
the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
items.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

items.headline: Flood Watch issued November 1 at 12:49PM EST until November 2 at 3:00PM EST by NWS Miami FL
items.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of southeast Florida, including the following
areas, Coastal Broward County, Coastal Miami Dade County, Coastal
Palm Beach County, Far South Miami-Dade County, Inland Broward
County, Inland Miami-Dade County, Inland Palm Beach County, Metro
Broward County, Metro Palm Beach County and Metropolitan Miami
Dade.

* WHEN...Through Monday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Isolated to scattered area of flash flooding will be
possible, with the main impact being street flooding, road
closures, and limited impact to structures in flood prone areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Uncertainty is high regarding exactly where the highest rain
amounts will fall. However, scattered locations across the east
coast may pick up 3 to 5 inches of rain through Monday. Isolated
spots may see accumulations as high as 5 to 7 inches. These
amounts may fall over a window of a few hours. Expected impacts
could be greater than forecast if the heaviest rainfall occurs
near the coast during times of high tide.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
items.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

items.headline: Small Craft Advisory issued November 1 at 1:19PM EST until November 3 at 10:00AM EST by NWS Miami FL
items.description:
* WHAT...East winds 20 to 25 kt and seas 5 to 8 ft.

* WHERE...Coastal waters from Jupiter Inlet to Deerfield Beach
FL out 20 NM, Coastal waters from Deerfield Beach to Ocean
Reef FL out 20 NM, Waters from Jupiter Inlet to Deerfield
Beach FL from 20 to 60 NM and Waters from Deerfield Beach to
Ocean Reef FL from 20 to 60 NM excluding the territorial
waters of Bahamas.

* WHEN...Until 10 AM EST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Conditions will be hazardous to small craft.
items.instruction:
Inexperienced mariners, especially those operating smaller
vessels, should avoid navigating in hazardous conditions.
